title: Leaf-script profile
description: A requester's prelude for the jobs of one leaf-script request (`script-request.schema.json`). `preamble` is program text emitted after the engine's guest shims and before every JavaScript job's own source; `preambleSha256` is its lower-case hex sha256 and is verified by the host before anything runs. A preamble that declares a name the engine or the envelope binds is refused. `hooks` names per-lane `prepare` functions the preamble defines, and is read by requesters, never by the runner. `python` carries a Python contract: a requester may unfold it into `python-project` jobs itself, or — where it carries `modes` — name a mode in the job and have the runner unfold it. Every byte of it is the requester's; the runner has no contract, no files and no modes of its own.

instructionSteps.description: Instruction budget for every job that sets none of its own. Unset: the engine default.

files.description: The files every evaluation of this contract carries, whatever the mode.

entry.description: The module whose top level runs. With `modes`, it must also be a Python module name and some file of the unfolded project must be it (`entry` or `entry.py`).

modes.description: The wrappings a job may name. Optional and purely additive: a profile without `modes` is the same profile it was, and a job without `modes` is the same job. Two modes of one name, a `block` that collides with a file, a `files` key that shadows `python.files`, or a mode whose project has no entry module are refused by the host (a JSON Schema cannot say them).

pythonMode.description: One wrapping of a job's `source` into a project. The runner merges `files` over `python.files`, writes `before` + the job's `source` + `after` to `block`, runs `python.entry`/`python.call`, and maps locations the engine reports in `block` back to the author's lines with `lineOffset`. It reads `name` as a lookup key and nothing else.

name.description: How a job names this wrapping. Unique within the profile.

files.description: Files this wrapping adds to `python.files` — the entry module among them. May not shadow a `python.files` key.

block.description: The file the wrapped source is written to, and the name the engine uses for it in a location. Not a key of `python.files` or of this mode's `files`.

before.description: Text placed before the job's `source` in `block`. May be empty.

after.description: Text placed after the job's `source` in `block`. May be empty.

lineOffset.description: Generated lines before the author's first line — the number of newlines in `before`. Engine line N in `block` is author line N - lineOffset, capped at the author's last line. Where `before` ends in a newline, N == lineOffset is author line 1 as well, because Python reports a multi-line statement at the line that opens it. Any line above that is left exactly as the engine wrote it: those lines are the wrapper's own and are not the author's to answer for. Columns are never adjusted (a `before` that does not end in a newline shifts the author's first line sideways, so a column there is the block's), and a character offset in a `(at offset K)` location is rebased by the UTF-16 length of `before`.

call.description: The function to call for this mode instead of `python.call`. A wrapping decides what the entry module defines: omit it where every mode answers the same way.
